institutionName: University of North Carolina at Greensboro

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture relating to my major. As I'm majoring in English, I wanted to surround myself with the English language in order to improve my spoken English. However, I also wanted to experience a culture that was very different from the Danish culture, and as I've been to England multiple times and find the culture quite similar to Danish culture, I opted to go to America instead.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy and there were people there to help and guide you in the first couple of days.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a guide on where and how to pick up the room key, and when I arrived to the building there was a student representative to greet me and help me get the key and student card.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were different student housings available, but I just went with Tower Village as it was where most international students were located.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were different meal plans, I just didn't understand the system before I came there and chose the "all inclusive" meal plan. It turns out that I could have gone for a much smaller meal plan and just cooked at home, but I wasn't aware of this when I signed up.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There's a kitchen in the individual apartments so if you want to cook at home, you can. Otherwise you'll have to walk 12-15 minutes to the cafeteria (if you live in Tower Village) every day, and that gets a bit tiring. Also, they aren't the most clean homes but you learn to live with it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it challenging, but that was probably just because of the difference in points etc. However, most of the professors are good at replying to your e-mails if you are in doubt about anything.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had misunderstood the level of courses that I was required to take, so I registered a bit late. This also meant that I ended up with two courses that weren't necessarily that interesting to me, but the two other courses were at the top of my priorities. I also ended up really enjoying one of the courses that weren't my first pick at the beginning.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: As said, the professors were generally pretty good at answering e-mails, and you also have your DSO (Dee) who can guide you a bit.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 50/50, I got two out of four that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you are 100% certain that the courses you want are at the level you need. So for example, I was required to ONLY take level 400 courses as I was a major in Denmark, but an undergraduate in USA, so all my courses would have the numbers 400-499. This is what I didn't understand in the beginning, and I chose courses from 300-499, which meant that I was "rejected" and had to choose new ones.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As said, I was on my second semester of the MA at UCPH, but because my grades weren't good enough to get nominated as a graduate student at UNCG, I had to take undergraduate courses. This is why I only had the options between 400-499 courses, which is kind of unusual as far as I could understand. Generally you'll have more room to choose different courses, my situation just limited my options.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was much more based on how you could apply what you learned in real life. I generally feel that UCPH teaching is based very much on academia, books, theories, etc. Although UNCG of course also applied theories to the learning, the assignments and final exams were focused more on personal experiences and how you could use those theories to explain some things that might go on in your own real life.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Family Communication (COMM), Communication and Friendship (COMM), African History and Cultures through Film (LLC), Environmental Justice (SWK)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the communication courses, the teachers were relatable, understandable, and prioritised including their students in the classroom. They used examples from their own personal lives which made it easy to relate to them and understand what they were trying to teach us.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: PayPal fees when transferring money to UNCG. Also, taxes in everything you buy, and tips for everyone.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was definitely very pricey given the state of the apartments.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of opportunities to watch sports games and other activities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basketball, soccer, tennis, softball, baseball, fitness, social gatherings in Tower Village, and much more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the sports games and just explore campus and downtown Greensboro. Take day trips to Charlotte, Wilmington, Charleston, etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Puerto Rico with a group of girls during Spring break and it was lovely. Go to bars and clubs downtown during the weekends; Limelight on Thursdays, Arizona Pete's on Fridays, Grey's Tavern on Saturdays, One Thirteen roof top whenever, Corner Bar and Jake's (close to campus). Go to all the states/cities that you want to see when you're there; it's not every day you get to go to the states. I recommend New York and Miami, but heard great things about Chicago and Tennessee as well. Go to Texas; if you go to Austin, make sure to live downtown as I went there and lived just in the outskirts which wasn't that nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time, but fortunately I had some really great roommates and friends who were there for me if I needed it. Definitely had to get used to the food as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to them whenever you can; during classes, in the cafeteria, at parties, etc. Unfortunately, I did notice that many students were kind of closed off during classes and sometimes difficult to approach.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that you basically had to have a car in order to go to shopping centers or Target/Walmart. Although there were busses, it wasn't always the easiest solution, and so I sometimes spent quite some money on Ubers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People didn't really seem to care about what other people thought about them. Coming from Denmark where people tend to be a little snobby and self-conceived, it was really freeing to be around people who didn't seem to care about what you're wearing or how you look in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Research your options for meal plans and housing; I do recommend Tower Village as most international students are there, but I could have saved quite a lot of money by cooking at home. Make sure that you are certain about what level of courses you need, so you don't end up having to do a late submission like I did. Socialize wherever you can; the connections I made with a lot of different people made my experience 100 times better. It also helps when you get homesick!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you get the meal plan "Unlimited 110", remember that you have 110 "Spartan Meals" that you can get around campus; EUC and Spartan Markets. Also make sure to use your flex money around campus; Bojangles, Chick-Fil-A, Panda Express, etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The development in my language and the friends I made there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling out of place at times, missing the people who know me 100%.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy it, time flies when you're there.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
